standard_prerequisites.name: The cohomology of a zero dimensional scheme and the structure of its degree zero part
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma describing the cohomology of a smooth projective scheme of dimension zero, including the dimension count and the identification of the degree zero part with a separable algebra
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the degree zero parts appearing in the tensor decomposition with products of coefficient fields.

standard_prerequisites.name: Additivity of the theory under disjoint unions
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma computing the cohomology of a disjoint union, together with axiom (B)(a) on the behaviour under products
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits the tensor product of the two degree zero parts according to the decomposition of the product of the spectra.

core_obligations: Split the tensor product (proof lines 3756-3768): writing the tensor product of the two finite separable algebras as a product of the larger one with a complementary finite separable algebra, and using the computation of the cohomology of zero dimensional schemes, the degree zero parts tensor to the product of the two corresponding coefficient algebras.

Compare the cohomologies (proof lines 3768-3784): the product of the two spectra is the disjoint union of the spectrum of the larger algebra and the spectrum of the complementary algebra, so the cohomology of the product is the product of the cohomologies of the base changes; the tensor decomposition of the degree zero parts identifies the tensor product of the cohomology of the scheme with the degree zero part as the cohomology of the base change, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the tensor product of the separable algebras.
Use additivity and the product formula to split the cohomology of the base change.
Read off the asserted identification of the tensor product.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for data satisfying all the axioms the cohomology of the base change of a smooth projective scheme along a finite separable algebra is the tensor product of the cohomology with the degree zero part of the spectrum of that algebra over the degree zero part of the base (statement lines 3752-3758). The proof (proof lines 3759-3784) decomposes the tensor product of the separable algebras and compares the two cohomologies through additivity and the product formula. H2: a complete short computation.
